data.description:
SURFACE: /submissions?sort=<unknown>

WHAT BREAKS: /submissions?sort=score_desc renders the page shell with an empty table and 'Submissions did not load - The system sent a request this conference could not accept... - ref a2a0da', and the sort dropdown renders with no option selected. A shareable/bookmarkable list view fails whole rather than degrading to a valid default.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed at live sha 75b871d94c6f):
- src/api/list.ts:43 -> sort: z.enum(sortKeys).default(options.defaultSort ?? sortKeys[0])
- .default() supplies a value when the key is MISSING; it does not catch an INVALID one. An unknown value therefore throws a ZodError -> 400 -> the list surface shows its load-failure state.
- Valid values are newest | updated | title | score | score_asc (src/routes/views.routes.ts:25). 'score_desc' is a plausible guess that is not in the whitelist -- exactly what an agent or a hand-edited URL produces.

FIX SHAPE: .catch(default) alongside .default(default) on the sort field in src/api/list.ts. Roughly one line, and it fixes every list endpoint built on the shared list contract at once.

WHY URGENT: cheap, and it is the failure mode an agent driving the product by URL hits first -- which bears directly on the 'agent-native by design' claim.

SIZE: trivial. No dependency.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, abstract-management judgement, defects[4]. Validated by reading live source.
data.title: An unrecognised sort value hard-errors the whole submissions list instead of falling back

data.body:
VALIDATION — driven in a real browser (c11 surface:37) against `npx vite dev` on a seeded local D1 (9,996 rows), not curl alone.

PREMISE CORRECTION, recorded because the ticket says otherwise: /submissions?sort=score_desc ALREADY RENDERS on current main. Commit d520c320 added normaliseSubmissionSort() in src/ui/submissions/list-request.ts, which rewrites an unknown sort before the request is assembled, and that commit IS in the deployed sha 75b871d9. Loaded pre-fix, the page showed a populated 1,000-row table with the sort dropdown reading 'Newest' — not the empty table and blank control the ticket describes. The triage read the source correctly; the client-side patch was simply newer than the report.

The defect underneath is real and has a live surface. PRE-FIX /people?sort=score_desc (no client normaliser) sits on its loading skeleton indefinitely, every stat reading '—', under the banner 'Your session has expired.' The session was fine. A 400 wearing an auth error's clothes.

PRE-FIX API: submissions?sort=score_desc -> 400, submissions?page=0 -> 400, org/people?sort=bogus -> 400.
POST-FIX API: all three -> 200.
POST-FIX UI: /people?sort=score_desc renders all 1,102 people; /submissions?sort=score_desc renders 1,000 records with the dropdown showing 'Newest' (screenshot taken, effective sort visible, control not blank). Strictness preserved: ?status=bogus still 400.

CAUGHT ONLY BY LOOKING: the first version of this fix passed its unit tests and 500'd the ENTIRE APP. .catch() is opaque to the OpenAPI generator — getOpenAPI31Document throws 'Unknown zod object type' while building the document and takes every route down with it. Found via an error overlay on the demo login in the browser, not by any red test. Each softened field now restates type/enum/minimum/maximum/default explicitly; the generated document is unchanged.

PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/128

PR #128 (the fix) was merged by BenevolentFutures at 21:11:47Z, ~6 minutes before my review-fix commit was pushed — so main has the core fix WITHOUT the two MINOR findings the code review raised. Follow-up PR #133 carries them, branched fresh off main: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/133

Both findings are small and neither changes behaviour today:
1. src/ui/submissions/list-request.ts comment said the API 'correctly refuses' an unknown sort — no longer true after #128. Rewritten to say why the client-side normalisation is still needed (the list envelope does not echo the applied sort, so the control would render blank).
2. createListQuerySchema's defaultSort was typed string with no membership check against sortKeys. #128 doubled down on that trust — the value now feeds the invalid-value path too, and Zod re-parses neither .default() nor .catch(). A guard now throws at module load. All current call sites are correct.

Review artifact: art_01KZVXBRRXEAHM23KZPCQAV6QT (verdict PASS).

MRQ-137 shipped to main in two PRs.

#128 (squash 769e44c9) — the fix. sort/page/per_page in the shared list contract (src/api/list.ts) now .catch() back to the endpoint's own defaults, which covers submissions, forms, board and comms at once; src/routes/people.routes.ts owns its own query schema and got the same treatment. Softening stops at navigation: q and every endpoint-owned filter stay strict, because answering a search with the unfiltered list returns a different set of records than the one asked for and the caller cannot see it happen. Caps still bind (per_page=101 -> 50, never past maxPerPage). Bulk selectors unaffected — src/api/bulk.ts reads neither page nor per_page, and sort cannot change which records a filter selects.

#133 (squash 39e81c19) — the two MINOR code-review findings. #128 was merged by BenevolentFutures ~6 minutes before my review-fix commit was pushed, so they needed their own PR off main. (1) The client-side normaliseSubmissionSort rationale said the API 'correctly refuses' an unknown sort — no longer true, and rewritten to say why the normalisation is still needed: the list envelope does not echo the applied sort, so the control would render blank without it. (2) createListQuerySchema's defaultSort was typed string with no membership check against sortKeys; #128 doubled down on that trust since the value now feeds the invalid-value path too, and Zod re-parses neither .default() nor .catch(). A guard now throws at module load. Both verified present on main.

TWO THINGS FUTURE TICKETS SHOULD INHERIT:

1. The ticket's premise was partly stale and this is worth remembering when triaging from a live sha. /submissions?sort=score_desc ALREADY rendered on main — commit d520c320 added a client-side normaliser that IS in the deployed sha 75b871d9. The defect was real but its live surface was /people?sort=score_desc, which has no normaliser: it sat on its loading skeleton forever, every stat reading '—', under a banner reading 'Your session has expired.' It had not. A 400 wearing an auth error's clothes is harder to diagnose than the dead end it replaces, and that mapping is still there for any other 400 the shell receives.

2. .catch() IS OPAQUE TO THE OPENAPI GENERATOR AND THIS IS A LANDMINE. It does not degrade the document — getOpenAPI31Document throws 'Unknown zod object type' while BUILDING it and takes every route down. The first version of this fix passed its unit tests and 500'd the entire app on its first request. Found only by loading the app in a browser; nothing went red. Any future .catch()/.transform() on a schema that reaches the OpenAPI document must restate type/enum/minimum/maximum/default explicitly via .openapi().

TESTS: tests/unit/api/list-sort-fallback.MRQ-137.test.ts (4 tests), verified failing pre-fix and passing after. tests/unit/api/list.test.ts (AC-108) asserted the old hard-failure contract; those assertions were flipped to the new behaviour with its filter-strictness assertion kept and strengthened. Test titles need an AC-<n> prefix, not MRQ-<n> — trace:ac enforces it.

GATE: npm run pr-gate status 'pass', 863/863 tests, 123/123 files, every check green. GitHub fast-gate SUCCESS on both PRs. Two earlier local runs went red with no failing assertion in different files each time; those files passed 8/8 in 47s isolated, at load ~210 on 16 cores. Running through .briefs/gate.sh is what made the difference.

VALIDATION: real browser (c11 surface:37) against npx vite dev on a seeded local D1 (9,996 rows). Pre-fix API 400s on all three URLs, post-fix all 200. /people?sort=score_desc renders 1,102 people; /submissions?sort=score_desc renders 1,000 records with the dropdown showing 'Newest' — the effective sort, not a blank control. ?status=bogus still 400s. Detail in the validation-role comment above.
